title: Failover Matrix Composer: 'What‑if' Latency & Cost Preview with Model‑Variant Diff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a Failover Matrix Composer in the Console that lets customers author region+tier routing policies and immediately preview the operational impact. The composer must show a tabular and timeline view of routing paths, simulated request distribution across regions/tiers/model variants, and a 'what‑if' cost and latency preview for a configurable workload (RPS, avg tokens, peak bursts). The UI should surface model‑variant diffs when a fallback is selected (e.g., fp16 -> int8 or smaller context window) and annotate expected quality regressions and token-cost delta. This ticket covers PM requirements, acceptance criteria, and coordination notes for Engineering and Design.
acceptance_criteria: Composer UI allows selection of primary region, fallback regions, tier order, and up to 3 fallback model variants per route

Preview engine simulates distribution for user‑provided workload parameters and returns: per-region latency P50/P95, estimated monthly token cost, and expected token savings from caching/batching suggestions
Model‑variant diff highlights delta in token cost, expected latency delta, and a quality-risk note sourced from existing evals (link to eval dashboard)
Validation runs prevent saving policies that violate tenant SLA constraints (configurable) and provide inline fix suggestions
Exportable scenario report (JSON + human-readable) for audit/engineering reproducibility
Console passes UX accessibility baseline and design has signoff from Design (DES-2311)
notes: Tradeoffs: accurate latency modeling requires telemetry from recent production runs vs. heuristics based on model profiles. For MVP we combine recent 7d median latency by region+model where available, else fall back to model profile
We decided to limit 'what‑if' preview compute to sampled simulations (configurable sample size) to keep responsive UX—full monte-carlo analysis will be separate offline job
Quality guidance will surfaced as a 3-level risk tag (low/medium/high) derived from evaluation diffs; engineering to add hooks to attach eval IDs
Must integrate with existing rollout/canary APIs so preview can show canary percentage split scenarios
Security: the export report should redact customer PII; Security review not required for MVP but will be re-evaluated if export adds logs
